about: Password proofs (protocol v2) from src/main/auth.js. proofs: full derivations; a viewer must reproduce key = scrypt(UTF-8(NFC(password)), base64-decoded salt, kdf) and proof = base64(HMAC-SHA256(key, message)), where message = context + nonce + "|" + hostId + "|" + viewerId and the nonce stays the base64 string. hmacVectors: proofs from a stored password record (stored = what the host keeps; proof = base64(HMAC-SHA256(base64-decoded stored.key, message))). functions: the auth.js function of that name. Regenerate with node scripts/make-mobile-fixtures.js.

computeProof.about: computeProof(password, {salt, kdf}, nonceB64, {hostId, viewerId}) rejects with error.code before running scrypt. The checks run in this order: binding, kdf, salt, nonce, password.

decodeB64.about: decodeB64(s, minBytes, maxBytes): strict, canonical standard base64 (salt 16..64, nonce 16..64, proof 32..32). Result: the bytes as lower-case hex, or null.

cases.note: 64 bytes: the longest salt or nonce

normalizeBinding.about: normalizeBinding({hostId, viewerId}) -> {hostId, viewerId} or null. Both must be Tailscale StableNodeIDs, /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/, compared exactly.

cases.note: "|" separates the fields of the HMAC message
an IP is not a node ID

validateKdf.about: validateKdf(kdf) -> bool. The viewer runs it on hello.auth.kdf before any scrypt.

cases.note: scrypt would need more than 64 MiB
scrypt would need more than 64 MiB
too little work: a rogue host could crack the proof cheaply
a string is not a number

verifyProof.about: verifyProof(stored, nonceB64, proofB64, {hostId, viewerId}) -> bool: the host side. stored = {salt, N, r, p, keylen, key}.

cases.note: relayed by another node: the host sees the relay as the viewer
bound to IPs instead of node IDs
nonce below 16 bytes (the proof matches it)

proofs.name: NFC: the precomposed e-acute gives vector 2
limits: 1024-unit password, 64-byte salt, 16-byte nonce, 64-character IDs, p = 2
